set(ORCASTRA_SRCS main.c fx.c vox.c synth.c drums.c viz.c keys.c
                  voice_data.c)   # GENERATED: flash-resident robot-voice sample

# ---- FW2App metadata contract ----------------------------------------------
# The BSP's app_about/app_recovery pair needs `fw2app_uf2_info` and
# `fw2app_repository_url`, generated by wilibsp's own tools/gen_uf2_info.py.
# It became MANDATORY for us the moment main.c started calling picpwr_task():
# that pulls in app_recovery.c -> app_about.c -> the metadata symbols, and the
# link fails with "undefined reference to fw2app_uf2_info".
#
# We invoke the generator directly rather than calling the BSP's
# fw2_display_app()/fw2_psram_app() wrappers, because those also install their
# own make_app_uf2.py POST_BUILD step and would collide with the picotool UF2
# conversion below. Adopting fw2_psram_app() wholesale is the right end state --
# it supplies an official PSRAM bootstrap, startup and linker scripts that would
# replace psram_xip_link entirely -- but that is a retooling to do deliberately,
# not mid-debug on the first build that actually launches. See AGENTS.md.
#
# NAME is what the on-device App Explorer shows. VERSION must be exactly three
# digits. DESCRIPTION is capped at 127 printable ASCII bytes, NAME at 31.
function(orcastra_app_metadata target)
    set(_dir "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/${target}_uf2_info")
    file(MAKE_DIRECTORY "${_dir}")
    add_custom_command(
        OUTPUT "${_dir}/${target}_uf2_info.c"
        COMMAND ${Python3_EXECUTABLE}
                "${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/../../wilibsp/tools/gen_uf2_info.py"
                --out "${_dir}/${target}_uf2_info.c"
                --version "1"
                --name "Orcastra"
                --description "FreeWili 2 audio multi-tool: synth, sampler, drums, theremin, FX chain"
                --repository "https://github.com/gtasseff/fw2-audio-demo"
        DEPENDS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/../../wilibsp/tools/gen_uf2_info.py"
        COMMENT "Generating FW2App metadata for ${target}"
        VERBATIM)
    target_sources(${target} PRIVATE "${_dir}/${target}_uf2_info.c")
    target_link_options(${target} PRIVATE -Wl,--undefined=fw2app_uf2_info)
endfunction()

# EVERY TARGET LOADS AT 0x11000000. Do not add one that loads into flash.
#
# QSPI flash at 0x10000000 holds the stock DISPLAY firmware, which is the
# bootloader that launches apps from the SD card. An image linked there and
# programmed over the debug probe replaces it, and this repository ships no
# image to restore it. Both targets below are therefore staged in PSRAM and
# routed by load address (AGENTS.md invariant 19).
#
# Apps are installed by copying the .uf2 to /apps on the card, or with
# wilibsp's `fw install-app`, which writes the card over MAIN's serial link.
# The debug probe remains the way to read RTT and to drive the agentio
# harness; neither writes to the device.

# The copy_to_ram target does not fit with the agentio harness linked in (~45 KB
# of SRAM against ~22 KB spare: '.bss will not fit in region RAM', overflowed by
# 16652 bytes). Skip it explicitly rather than letting the link fail, so
# -DFW2_AGENTIO=ON reports a deliberate omission instead of an error.
if(FW2_AGENTIO)
    message(STATUS "FW2_AGENTIO=ON: skipping orcastra_sd "
                   "(copy_to_ram + harness exceeds SRAM); building orcastra_psram only")
endif()

if(NOT FW2_AGENTIO)
# SD-card twin for the stock launcher's /apps picker. Same sources, same
# copy_to_ram execution-from-SRAM behaviour; the ONLY difference is that the
# load image sits in PSRAM at 0x11000000 instead of flash at 0x10000000, which
# is what makes the stock loader stage it and jump rather than overwrite the
# DISPLAY firmware. The reasoning is in psram_link/pico_flash_region.ld -- read
# it before touching either file.
set(ORCASTRA_SD_SRCS ${ORCASTRA_SRCS})
list(REMOVE_ITEM ORCASTRA_SD_SRCS voice_data.c)   # sidecar'd - see sd_entry.c/main.c
add_executable(orcastra_sd ${ORCASTRA_SD_SRCS} sd_entry.c)
target_link_libraries(orcastra_sd freewili2_bsp pico_multicore)
orcastra_app_metadata(orcastra_sd)
# Launched-app contract (see sd_entry.c): never re-probe the PSRAM window we
# were staged through. The SWD/flash orcastra target keeps the SDK init - a
# cold boot genuinely needs it.
target_compile_definitions(orcastra_sd PRIVATE PICO_RUNTIME_SKIP_INIT_PSRAM=1
                           ORCASTRA_SD_BOOT_TRACE=1
                           ORCASTRA_SD_NO_VOICE=1)
pico_set_binary_type(orcastra_sd copy_to_ram)
pico_add_linker_script_override_path(orcastra_sd ${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/psram_link
                                     FILES pico_flash_region.ld pico_psram_region.ld)

# NOT pico_add_extra_outputs(): its ELF->UF2 step fails with "entry point is not
# in mapped part of file", because picotool drops segments it cannot place for
# the family and the PSRAM entry point is then in no emitted block. Convert from
# the flat .bin with an explicit load address instead -- the blocks are what the
# stock loader reads, and they must carry 0x11000000.
pico_add_bin_output(orcastra_sd)
pico_init_picotool()
add_custom_command(TARGET orcastra_sd POST_BUILD
    COMMAND picotool ARGS uf2 convert
            ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/orcastra_sd.bin -t bin
            ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/orcastra_sd.uf2
            -o 0x11000000 --family rp2350-arm-s
    BYPRODUCTS ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/orcastra_sd.uf2
    VERBATIM
    COMMENT "Packaging orcastra_sd.uf2 for the /apps PSRAM path (blocks -> 0x11000000)")
endif()  # NOT FW2_AGENTIO

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# orcastra_psram: EXECUTE from PSRAM instead of copying to SRAM.
#
# This mirrors a known-good production build of the same app, which was
# analysed binary-first to work out the scheme; the evidence trail is in
# psram_xip_link/pico_flash_region.ld.
#
# The ONLY structural difference from orcastra_sd is the ABSENCE of
# pico_set_binary_type(... copy_to_ram): with the default binary type, .text and
# .rodata get VMA == LMA in the FLASH region -- which psram_xip_link retargets to
# 0x11000000 -- so they execute in place from PSRAM, and crt0 copies only .data
# into SRAM. That single omission is the fix.
#
# WHY: SRAM, not speed. copy_to_ram spends ~125 KB of SRAM on the image, and
# .bss is already 368 KB, leaving 22.6 KB spare -- with an arpeggiator specced
# and unbuilt. This scheme spends ~29 KB instead. Latency is NOT a reason to
# avoid it: a build using this scheme was demoed and latency-measured on
# hardware with no audible penalty, which is empirical evidence that
# XIP-from-PSRAM meets the 5.2 ms capture deadline.
#
# The voice sample is baked back IN here (no ORCASTRA_SD_NO_VOICE): with code in
# PSRAM there is room for the 83 KB array, so the voice.bin sidecar and its
# VOX1 header contract are simply unnecessary for this target.
#
# VERIFIED ON HARDWARE: launches from the /apps picker on a production unit,
# executes from PSRAM at 250 MHz, codec and sampler both live.
#
# It took four attempts to get there, and the first three all hung the same
# way -- see sd_entry.c, where the actual cause is documented: the SDK's
# runtime_init_early_resets() resets IO_BANK0, which strips PSRAM's
# chip-select function off its GPIO, so the very next instruction fetch
# bus-faults. If you are debugging a silent hang here, start there.
#
# Keep running tools/check_psram_xip.py after ANY change to the linker
# scripts or the source list: it asserts the properties that make this build
# safe, and several of them fail silently on hardware rather than at link.
add_executable(orcastra_psram ${ORCASTRA_SRCS} sd_entry.c)
target_link_libraries(orcastra_psram freewili2_bsp pico_multicore)
orcastra_app_metadata(orcastra_psram)
# Same launched-app contract as orcastra_sd (see sd_entry.c): never re-probe the
# PSRAM window we were staged through. Doubly true here - it holds our code.
target_compile_definitions(orcastra_psram PRIVATE PICO_RUNTIME_SKIP_INIT_PSRAM=1
                           ORCASTRA_SD_BOOT_TRACE=1
                           ORCASTRA_PSRAM_INHERIT_TIMING=1)
# Inherit the loader stub's PSRAM timing instead of re-timing it: re-timing the
# chip we are executing from left it non-responsive and locked the CPU up on the
# first hardware test. Full evidence in sd_entry.c next to
# __wrap_psram_reinitialize().
target_link_options(orcastra_psram PRIVATE -Wl,--wrap=psram_reinitialize)
# PSRAM tCPH is NOT set here. It is consumed by board_init() in the BSP, which
# compiles once into the shared freewili2_bsp static library, so a PRIVATE define
# on this target cannot reach it -- verified by disassembly (`movs r2, #18`, the
# SDK default, survived a per-target define). It lives in the top-level
# CMakeLists.txt instead; see PICO_DEFAULT_PSRAM_MIN_DESELECT there.
# NO pico_set_binary_type() call. That omission IS the change.
pico_add_linker_script_override_path(orcastra_psram
                                     ${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/psram_xip_link
                                     FILES pico_flash_region.ld
                                           pico_psram_region.ld
                                           default_text_excludes.incl)
pico_add_bin_output(orcastra_psram)
add_custom_command(TARGET orcastra_psram POST_BUILD
    COMMAND picotool ARGS uf2 convert
            ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/orcastra_psram.bin -t bin
            ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/orcastra.uf2
            -o 0x11000000 --family rp2350-arm-s
    BYPRODUCTS ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/orcastra.uf2
    VERBATIM
    COMMENT "Packaging orcastra.uf2 (executes from PSRAM @ 0x11000000)")
# NOTE the artifact is orcastra.uf2, not orcastra_psram.uf2: the on-device App
# Explorer lists FILENAMES, not the FW2App metadata name, so the file itself has
# to carry the product name. The CMake TARGET keeps its _psram suffix because the
# suffix describes the execution model, which is what a developer needs to know.
